subject: Meridian3b 503/timeout pattern — customer impact & recovery steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-05T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Meridian3b 503 spike — initial ops alert

Folks,

Pager triggered at 09:08 PT — a subset of Meridian3b endpoints started returning 503s and a rise in backend timeouts for requests with ctx >= 4096 tokens. We’ve isolated the pattern to a specific inference shard pool (pool-id: m3b-eu-021) that is heterogeneously responding with 503s under sustained tail-latency pressure. Impact so far: ~2.4% error rate on ACME routes (traffic routed via us-west fallback) and higher latency for long-context sessions.

I’m attaching a short sample log and the quick mitigation playbook. Initial mitigation applied: circuit-breaker lowered for the pool and routing temporarily shifted to the warm fallback pool; that reduced 503s to ~0.5% but some long requests still time out.

Next steps I suggest: 1) notify the customer with a brief incident update, 2) escalate to PS for any client-side retry guidance, and 3) schedule a deeper kernel/kv-cache trace for the shard.

Priyom

Attachments: meridian3b-error-sample.log (excerpt), mitigation-playbook.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Meridian3b 503 spike — initial ops alert

Samantha — we’re seeing an elevated 5xx rate and intermittent timeouts for the Meridian3b model on a small subset of capacity. We wanted to let you know as soon as we confirmed it and to share immediate mitigation steps we’ve implemented:

- Shifted ACME traffic away from the affected shard pool to a warm fallback pool.
- Lowered circuit-breaker threshold on the problematic pool and applied per-account retry hints.
- Increased aggressive prefix cache retention for long-context requests to reduce kernel pressure.

Current status: error rate downgraded from ~2.4% to ~0.5% for your account, but a small number of long-context requests may still see elevated latency or timeouts. Our SRE (Marcus) and Ops (Priyom) are digging in; I’ve included a mitigation playbook and a short log excerpt for transparency.

We’ll keep you updated as we have a root cause and a timeline for full recovery. For now, recommended customer-side actions: short retry with jitter for idempotent calls and limit single-request context size where feasible.

Please reply if you’re seeing production user impact beyond what we described.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-10-05T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Meridian3b 503 spike — initial ops alert

Thanks Lauren — we did see a brief uptick in internal error dashboards starting ~09:25 PT, mostly on night-batch inference jobs hitting 6k token spans. Impact summary from our side: ~1.8% failed jobs (retries cleared many), and 0.2% upstream customer-facing requests returned an error.

Two asks: 1) can you confirm whether this affected any persisted user sessions (we rely on sticky sessions for session affinity), and 2) do you have a rough ETA for full mitigation / follow-up RCA?

We appreciate the quick mitigation. Keeping us in the loop helps our on-call routing.

Samantha
Customer Engineering Manager, Acme Cloud
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2028-10-05T11:50:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Meridian3b 503 spike — initial ops alert

Lauren / team — quick technical update to share with ACME and for our internal ticket:

Root of the behavior (initial hypothesis): an allocator imbalance combined with a new attention kernel path that regresses under >4k context when certain kv-cache eviction patterns align. The affected shard pool saw periodic GC-like stalls in the local allocator manifesting as transient 503s under tail load.

Immediate actions taken:
- Hotfix: disabled the new kernel path on pool m3b-eu-021; fallbacks to the stable kernel immediately.
- Rebalanced allocator quotas across the pool and drained the hottest nodes for warm-up.
- Raised active shard headroom for ACME routes for 2 hours.

Expected outcome: these changes should materially reduce timeouts for long-context sessions. We'll collect traces over the rest of the day and schedule a full replay test tomorrow.

I recommend we offer Acme a post-incident runbook + a courtesy credit for the affected window.

Marcus
Sr SRE, Inference Runtime

Subject: Meridian3b 5xx incident — recovery confirmation & next steps

Samantha — quick follow-up now that we’ve completed the immediate remediation and an initial RCA:

What we did:
- Reverted the new kernel path for the affected shard pool and rebalanced allocator quotas (Oct 5, 11:10 PT).
- Drained/rehomed hot nodes and increased headroom for heavy-context jobs.
- Added an interim guardrail: requests with context >6k tokens are now routed to a low-concurrency tier that guarantees stable kernel execution until we fully validate the new path.

Result: Meridian3b error rates for your routed traffic are back to baseline (<0.1% 5xx) as of Oct 7, 15:00 PT. We observed no lost persisted sessions attributable to this incident (we double-checked session affinity logs).

What’s next:
- We’ll publish a short postmortem (link below) with timeline, root cause, and permanent remediation plan; ETA: Oct 9.
- Offer: a service credit for the impacted window (HS-12345). I’ve looped in PS to coordinate any customer-side retry guidance.
- Long-term: fix & revalidate the new kernel path with extended replay tests and add synthetic long-context traffic to our CI gating.

Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.com/postmortems/meridian3b-20281007
Ticket: HS-12345

Appreciate the patience and the quick coordination — let me know if you want a short 15-min sync tomorrow to walk through the timeline.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
